transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
The architect of Tennessee's lethal injection protocols is stepping down from his position
after the state's second botched execution this year.
Marianna Bacchiao has more from member station WPLN in Nashville.
Frank Strada helped design the state's new execution process after a 2020 review found
that Tennessee had not properly inspected the drugs it uses to put people to death.
Strada came to Tennessee from Arizona, where he oversaw three botched executions similar
to Wednesday's.
Christa Pike did not die after receiving two full doses of pentobarbital.
Usually just one dose is considered lethal.
Pike's attorneys say she is unconscious and on a ventilator at an area hospital following
Wednesday's botched execution.
For NPR News, I'm Marianna Bacchiao in Nashville.
Business owners across the U.S. say the high cost of diesel fuel in the country right now
is hurting their profitability.
G7 Nations agreed this week to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel with
the hope of relieving price pressures in the U.S.
Mark St. Clair owns a pool cleaning company in Sandusky, Ohio.
He says the move is a temporary solution for a larger problem.
We do so many calls a day, you know, these trucks are on the road six days a week and
it's just our costs are going up, up, up.
And it's almost to the point where we've got to raise all of our prices to the customers.
The U.S. Coast Guard is searching the waters south of Nantucket, Massachusetts right now
for a Canadian air ambulance that disappeared early Saturday morning while traveling from
Bermuda to Boston.
And Piers Frank Langford has more on our story.
The Gulfstream G-100 is believed to have been carrying six people on board when it lost
contact with air traffic control, according to the Coast Guard.
Flight data show the jet dropped at least 9,000 feet over two minutes, then leveled
off for several more minutes before disappearing.
The pilot declared an emergency, according to Nantucket Memorial Airport.
During an exchange, air traffic control asked the pilot of the air ambulance, quote, "You're
coming in blind," a fire rescue dispatcher warned emergency crews, the plane was suffering
from electrical issues and had lost radio and radar, according to audio on broadcastify,
and that was also reviewed by the Boston Globe.
The Coast Guard has deployed two search and rescue planes, as well as a helicopter and
a motor lifeboat.
Frank Langford, NPR News.
President Trump was in Dayton, Ohio on Saturday to rally voters there in advance of November's
midterm elections.
He arrived just days after more than 1,300 people were laid off at a nearby truck factory.
He promoted his administration's actions on data centers, saying he wanted them to
benefit local communities.
Ohio is a center of protest over those centers.
Activists say data centers in Ohio have raised the price of electricity by as much as 30 percent
over the past few years.
You're listening to NPR News.
The U.S. says citizens needing help in Brazil should not come to its embassy or other consular
facilities right now.
This unusual suspension comes as Brazilians go to the polls in a presidential contest,
NPR's Kerry Conn reports.
Citing unspecified security concerns, the U.S. announced the closure of its diplomatic
missions beginning Friday.
The U.S. State Department did not say what prompted the closures, nor when consular services
would resume operations.
Federal police in Brazil said they had not found evidence of a threat after carrying
out preventative searches in Sao Paulo and near Brasilia.
The presidential race pits incumbent leftist Luis Anacio Lula da Silva against conservative
Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, who's under house
arrest for plotting a coup.
Crime and corruption are high on voters' list of main issues as well as U.S. relations and
its intensified interventions in Brazilian affairs.
Kerry Conn, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.
Josh Hoover threw for 251 yards and four touchdowns Saturday as No. 6 Indiana thrashed Rutgers
47-15.
Turbo Richard had a career-high 204 rushing yards in the win.
No. 3 Notre Dame struggled against North Carolina but managed a 37-26 win while No. 4 Miami easily
handled Clemson 41-13.
No. 7 Alabama struggled in the first half before beating Mississippi State 56-23 while
No. 8 Florida was dominated by No. 25 Missouri losing 45-17.
And Bloomsburg beat the Lackawanna Falcons by a score of 42-10.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
This message comes from Charles Schwab with their original podcast, Choiceology, hosted
by Katie Milkman, an award-winning behavioral scientist and author of the best-selling book,
How to Change.
Choiceology is a show about the psychology and economics behind people's decisions.
Learn true stories from Nobel laureates, historians, authors, athletes, and more about why people
do the things they do.
Download the latest episode and subscribe at Schwab.com/podcast or wherever you listen.

U.S. Coast Guard searches waters south of Nantucket for missing Canadian air ambulance
Canadian air ambulance carrying six people lost contact with air traffic control Saturday

Trump promotes data center administration actions while Ohio protests rising electricity prices

Brazil holds presidential election between incumbent Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro
